$comment: Pinned inputs for the Clang-WASM toolchain. Verify with `node build-memfs.mjs --verify-only`.

memfs.why: The memfs blob in binji/wasm-clang is byte-identical (345,442 bytes) to the one shipped by @chriskoch/cpp-wasm and @wasm-idle/llvm-core, so this is the published module's source.

license.note: memfs.c carries no per-file license header. Containing repos: binji/wasm-clang is Apache-2.0; binji/llvm-project is Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception. stb_sprintf.h is stb (public domain / MIT). We modify memfs.c, so Apache-2.0 section 4(b) applies: ship a notice that the file was changed. Confirm with the author before relying on this, since the file itself is unmarked.

toolchain.name: wasi-sdk
toolchain.note: Pin this version. memfs.c is 2020 code and the build relies on mechanical WASI renames; a future wasi-sdk may rename more. Re-run the feature verification when bumping.

patches.why: the capacity fix this rebuild exists for
errno constants gained ERRNO_ infix (9 constants)

patches.what: __wasi_filestat_t st_* fields lose prefix; __wasi_prestat_t pr_type -> tag

patches.why: libc abort reaches __wasi_proc_exit, a wasi_snapshot_preview1 import the runtime does not satisfy

memfs.wasm.gz.measured: drove the module directly; traps on node 4092

sysroot.why: The shipped sysroot reports _LIBCPP_VERSION 220100. At this tag all 825 shared files are byte-identical to it, so the sysroot is a pure prune with zero modifications.

hosted.why: The three compiler assets that are served rather than built here. They are copied into packages/clang-wasm/assets/ so the npm package needs no host of its own, and these receipts are what proves the copy is the one that was checked.
hosted.provenance: Unlike memfs and the sysroot, which this repository builds, and the Objective-C runtime, whose receipts the wasm-idle app publishes, these three were measured from the mirror on 2026-09-17. The manifest is also pinned upstream in the app's clangAssetIntegrity.ts; clang.wasm.gz and lld.wasm.gz are not published with a receipt we can check against, so their hashes are trust-on-first-use. Re-measure and update them if the mirror is ever repointed.

objectiveC.discoveredVia: @wasm-idle/llvm-core/objective-c declares the six asset names; the receipts are the ones its own app pins in its bundle (clangAssetIntegrity), and all six were re-verified byte-for-byte against these URLs.
objectiveC.why: Objective-C is not a Clang flag: the program links a runtime, and libobjc2's load function needs a constructor the Clang runtime's link line does not emit. These are the assets @wasm-idle/llvm-core/objective-c expects.

license.libgnustep-base.a: LGPL-2.1-or-later (GNUstep Base). Object code, so redistributing it triggers the corresponding-source obligation of LGPL sections 4 and 6 - the reason it is not in the npm package.
license.libgnustep-base.o: LGPL-2.1-or-later (GNUstep Base), object code, and not fetched by the runtime either.
license.foundation-headers.json: Mixed. 168 of its 262 files carry the GNUstep Base LGPL-2.1-or-later notice, with 'or any later version' and no linking exception; the rest are system and third-party headers bundled alongside. This one is source rather than object code, so redistributing it needs the licence text and the intact notices, not corresponding source.

objectiveC.licensing: See THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md at the repository root for the full list and for the LGPL obligation that comes with keeping the GNUstep Base files in .asset-cache. The licence text itself is in LICENSES/LGPL-2.1.txt.
objectiveC.delivery: Three of the six are published only gzipped at <name>.gz; the loader retries that path and inflates it, verifying the decoded bytes. serve.mjs mirrors them so the uncompressed path works too, and re-serves them with content-encoding: gzip to keep the wire cost compressed.
objectiveC.used: Only libobjc.a and headers.json are fetched: they are the whole cost of plain Objective-C, 273503 bytes. The other four belong to the installer's Foundation path (GNUstep Base + libffi), which is not usable here - see README. The integrity map still has to carry all six, because the installer validates the receipt of every asset name it declares.

wire.with Foundation (not usable here): + 4671198 (libgnustep-base.a.gz) + 313306 (foundation-headers.json.gz) + 4966 (libffi.a) = 5.3 MB on the wire, 17.1 MB decoded

memfsNodes.note: Only what the mounted headers.json needs: 25 files + 2 directories. Foundation's foundation-headers.json would add 1 more at load, inlining the rest. Neither is a constraint against 4091 usable nodes - the Objective-C runtime was never why the producer shipped a pruned sysroot.

thirdPartySources.why: The .asset-cache mirror redistributes GNUstep Base (LGPL-2.1-or-later) in object-code form, so the corresponding source has to be available from the same place. These are the sources committed for that, and third-party-sources/README.md is the long version.

gnustep-base.component: GNUstep Base, the library behind .asset-cache/objective-c/libgnustep-base.a, libgnustep-base.o and foundation-headers.json
gnustep-base.howIdentified: Read out of the artifacts, because nothing publishes it: GNUSTEP_BASE_VERSION 13101 with MAJOR 1 / MINOR 31 / SUBMINOR 1 in the shipped GNUstepBase/preface.h, corroborated by the '1.31' string and the clang_22.1.0-wasi-sdk marker inside libgnustep-base.a.
gnustep-base.configuredHeaders: third-party-sources/gnustep-base-1.31.1-configured/ holds config.h, GSConfig.h, GNUstepBase/config.h, GNUstepBase/GSConfig.h and GNUstepBase/preface.h as built, taken from foundation-headers.json. The tarball has the .in templates for four of them.
gnustep-base.match: 201 of the 262 headers in foundation-headers.json are byte-identical to Source/ or Headers/ in this tarball, 0 differ, 5 are configure-generated (shipped separately), and 56 are other projects' headers bundled alongside (libffi 3.6.0, the blocks runtime, libdispatch, curl, libc and system headers) - all permissive.
gnustep-base.notIncluded: wasm_llvm_foundation_support.o, the producer's own object inside libgnustep-base.a (1 of 219 members, symbols including GSWasmLlvmInitializeNSStringCluster), together with the exact configure flags and any patches. The wasm-llvm build repository is not public - it is named by @wasm-idle/llvm-core's README but appears on neither GitHub nor npm - so what is committed is the upstream corresponding source, not a byte-for-byte recipe for the archive.
